title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed an artifact-backed paired experiment that measures whether inserting a selective low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) into a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated configuration proposals while satisfying an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired operator intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed: baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975), guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Model-call accounting reflects the preregistered shared-initial design: planned budget enumerated 800 model generations but observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial generations + 1 repair). The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry was not recorded in the archived confirmatory artifacts; we disclose that absence and provide full provenance for all archived raw outputs, validator traces, per-episode scorer JSONs, and provider-call logs (SHA‑256 cataloged in the execution manifest). We discuss the ceiling effect on detectability, the implications of the shared-initial design, and reproducibility paths for follow-up runs that record latency telemetry and expand model/validator diversity.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation can dramatically reduce operator effort but introduces operational risk when generated proposals are incorrect or produce regressions. The canonical mitigation is a generate–validate–repair pipeline in which an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, an automated verifier (digital twin / formal checker) validates correctness, and an automated repair or human escalation occurs when the verifier fails. Full verification is often costly in latency-sensitive workflows. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to measure whether a selective, low-latency verification tier—risk-scoring shared LLM candidates and sending only high-risk proposals to a fast verifier—reduces unsafe commits compared with an LLM-only baseline, and whether it meets a latency SLO. The study was run autonomously per the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher requirements; all model outputs, scorer JSONs, provider-call logs, validator traces, manifests, and hashes are archived (execution manifest). The manuscript reports only artifact-backed numbers; missing preregistered telemetry (latency) is disclosed and not imputed.
Contributions: (1) a preregistered, paired confirmatory evaluation of a selective verifier intervention for NetOps LLM pipelines with full archival provenance; (2) reproducible reconciliation of planned vs observed model-call accounting under a preregistered shared-initial design; (3) artifact-grounded analysis showing a near-ceiling baseline and discussing operational interpretation and next-step experiments.
sections.related_work: Prior work studies LLM-driven configuration generation, verifier-augmented repair loops, and agentic NetOps. Recent benchmarks and studies (examples included in our evidence bundle) examine LLM-powered configuration repair at scale and agentic verifier-augmented architectures (see Cornetto-like configuration-repair benchmarks and agentic evaluation papers). Formal network verification, digital-twin validation, and hybrid generate–validate repair methods provide the methodological foundation we reuse here. Our study differs by preregistering the paired confirmatory design, rigorously archiving all per-episode artifacts and provider-call logs, and reconciling model-call accounting under a shared-initial candidate design. Representative nearest-work items archived with this run include (artifact-backed citations): Cornetto-style benchmarking and configuration-repair studies (arXiv:2604.22513), agentic verifier-augmented evaluation (arXiv:2606.06212), and agentic NetOps with digital twin validation (arXiv:2604.18233). We position our contribution as an operationally precise, provenance-rich complement to those works.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design
- Preregistration: CAND-2026-001 preregistered the research question, confirmatory hypotheses (H1 safety; H2 latency SLO), sampling plan, retry and missingness policy, estimator definitions, and analysis scripts (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration artifact SHA‑256 is recorded in the evidence bundle.
- Corpus and tasks: 400 deterministic paired intents were generated by a reproducible synthetic-task generator covering representative NetOps changes (ACLs, routing, interface edits). Ten percent (40/400) are preregistered adversarial/OOD variants (deterministic perturbations). Task manifests, reference answers, and per-task metadata are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Representative task example: pair-000001 manifest and responses archived at execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA-256: ea8359dbe5a5d054278e24f3...).
Intervention and baseline
- Baseline: LLM-only candidate accepted (no selective verification). Guarded (intervention): risk scorer + fast verifier evaluated candidate and—if flagged—applied a fast deterministic validation/repair step prior to final scoring by the deterministic full-checker. The pipeline, scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation), and deterministic validator id (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were preregistered and archived.
Shared-initial design and model-call accounting
- To isolate verifier/repair effects and limit stochastic generator variance, the preregistration allowed a shared-initial candidate per intent reused across conditions (independent_condition_generation=false). This choice was preregistered and executed. Planned_model_calls enumerated 800 under an independent-generation accounting convention, but the executed shared-initial run used 401 model calls (400 shared-initial + 1 repair). The deterministic reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) documents these counts and the provider-call audit; all provider-call traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/ with SHA‑256 entries.
Scoring, validator, and outcome definitions
- Per-episode outcomes (binary: valid/unsafe with respect to the deterministic full-checker) were produced by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and stored as per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json). The primary estimand is the paired difference in valid-proposal rate (guarded − baseline). Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided; confidence interval via paired bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Missingness and retry rules were preregistered and followed; there were no unrecovered infrastructure failures.
Reproducibility
- All raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), validator traces (execution/responses/*-validator), provider-call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifests, and model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (cataloged in execution manifest). Analysts can deterministically reproduce the reported tables and contingency counts from those artifacts.
sections.results:
Confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed)
- Completed pairs: 400 (complete_pair_count = 400). See analysis/condition_summary.csv (execution artifact: SHA-256 0d6efc16...).
- Baseline valid proposals: 399/400 (0.9975).
- Guarded valid proposals: 400/400 (1.000).
- Paired contingency table (guarded × baseline): n11 = 399, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256 a6906bb4...).
- Primary estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).
Model-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation
- Planned model-call budget enumerated in preregistration used an independent-generation accounting convention (800 generations). The executed run followed the preregistered shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false), producing one shared candidate per intent and reusing it across conditions; model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair). The deterministic reconciliation is archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) and the provider-call audit in the execution manifest documents stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":400, "repair":1} and provider-call logs under execution/provider_calls/.
Representative discordant episode (artifact mapping)
- The sole discordant pair (n10 = 1: guarded valid, baseline invalid) is available for inspection in the archived scorer JSONs: execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA-256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA-256: d0cbfe9a...). The per-episode validator traces show the baseline candidate failed a dependency check while the guarded pipeline selected/applied a corrected candidate prior to final scoring; artifacts contain the exact validator trace and the shared-initial candidate SHA for inspection.
Latency SLO (H2)
- The preregistered H2 required artifact-backed end-to-end latency telemetry to determine 95th-percentile pipeline latency. The confirmatory artifact bundle does not include the required end-to-end latency traces. Consequently, H2 could not be evaluated from the archived run; this missingness is logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We report H2 as unresolved rather than imputed.
sections.discussion:
Quantitative interpretation
- The observed primary effect is a small absolute improvement (0.25 percentage points). With a near-ceiling baseline (399/400), statistical power to detect small improvements is limited; the exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrapped CI [0.0, 0.0075] quantify this uncertainty. The result should be read as: under the preregistered corpus, model, deterministic validator, and shared-initial candidate protocol, guarded selective verification did not produce a statistically significant safety gain beyond an already-high baseline.
Operational implications
- When baseline LLM generation performance is already near ceiling for the evaluation validator, the operational return from a selective fast verifier is necessarily small; resources invested in verification may be better spent on adversarial-OOD detection, larger corpora, or model/validator diversification. Conversely, in settings with lower generator reliability or higher adversarial risk, selective verification is likely to yield larger, operationally meaningful safety benefits.
Design trade-offs: shared-initial vs independent-generation
- The shared-initial design (preregistered) reduces variance due to generator nondeterminism and isolates verifier/repair effect conditional on a single generated candidate; it also materially reduced model calls (observed 401). However, it changes the estimand: our paired difference answers whether the verifier/repair pipeline improves validity conditional on the same generated candidate, not the joint effect of independently re-sampling generator outputs per condition. Both estimands are operationally relevant in different workflows; we document this design choice and provide deterministic reconciliation artifacts for reviewers.
Failure modes and example inspection
- The one discordant example (n10=1) demonstrates a common failure mode: a baseline candidate violated a dependency that the guarded pipeline corrected. That per-episode evidence is archived (execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json: SHA-256 fe147f43...; execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json: SHA-256 d0cbfe9a...). Analysts can replay the provider-call traces and validator traces to inspect exactly which check was violated and how the guarded pipeline mitigated it.
Reproducibility and provenance
- All reported numbers are reproducible from archived artifacts: raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifests, model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json), execution/execution_log.jsonl, and analysis artifacts. Key artifact hashes are recorded in the execution manifest and in the Disclosure Statement below.
Open empirical gaps
- The preregistered latency SLO could not be evaluated due to absent timing telemetry; any operational claim about meeting the 2000 ms SLO would be unsupported. Future runs must record and archive per-stage timestamps (generation, risk scoring, fast verifier, full-checker) to validate latency targets.
Recommendations for follow-up artifact-grounded experiments
1) Record end-to-end telemetry and preregister the latency analysis to test H2. 2) Repeat with independent_condition_generation=true to measure joint generator+verifier effects. 3) Sweep selective-threshold risk budgets with a larger adversarial/OOD portion to map the verification-budget vs unsafe-commit Pareto frontier. 4) Variant studies across LLM families and validators to assess external validity; all artifacts should be archived with SHA‑256 as done here.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, provenance-rich paired experiment evaluating selective low-latency verification in LLM-driven NetOps pipelines. Under the preregistered synthetic corpus, single model (gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator, and shared-initial candidate design, the guarded intervention produced a numerically small absolute safety gain (0.25 percentage points) over a very-high baseline; this effect is artifact-backed but not statistically distinguishable from zero given the near-ceiling baseline and the observed discordance pattern. The preregistered latency target could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry was not archived for the confirmatory run; we disclose this limitation and provide full execution provenance to enable reproducible follow-up runs that record timing and broaden model/validator conditions. All raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and paths in the execution manifest for independent verification and deeper failure-mode analysis.

limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: deterministic generator tasks may not capture the full linguistic diversity of operator intents in production.
Single-model scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize to other LLM families without further testing.
Single deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 is a digital-twin style checker; real-device divergences may remain.

Shared-initial design: the chosen conditional estimand (shared-initial candidate per intent) isolates verifier/repair effects but differs from an independent-generation estimand (independent candidate per condition).
Latency SLO unresolved: required per-stage end-to-end latency telemetry for H2 was not archived; H2 is therefore unresolved in this run.
